name: OPA2188AIDR
title: OPA2188: dual 36-V zero-drift, low-noise op amp with rail-to-rail output
summary: The OPA2188 holds two auto-zeroing precision op amps in one SOIC-8 or VSSOP-8 package, with 25 µV maximum offset, 0.085 µV/°C maximum drift and 8.8 nV/√Hz noise at 1 kHz. It runs from 4 V to 36 V (±2 V to ±18 V) at 415 µA typical per amplifier, has a 2 MHz gain-bandwidth product, a CMOS input whose range includes the negative rail, and an output that swings within 15 mV of the rails. It is specified from -40°C to +105°C.

circuits.title: High-side voltage-to-current converter
circuits.description: Turns 0 V to 2 V at VIN into 0 mA to 100 mA sourced from a 5 V rail into a grounded load. Amplifier A drives N-channel Q1 through R3 so that VIN appears across RS1, setting a current of VIN / RS1 that Q1 pulls through RS2 from the rail; C6 runs from its output to its inverting input, which R2 ties to the RS1 node. Amplifier B compares the drop across RS2 with the drop across the 4.7 Ω RS3, and drives the gate of P-channel Q2 through R5 until the two match, so the load current through Q2 is the first-stage current scaled by RS2 / RS3. R4 and C7 form its feedback from the RS3 node.

parts.note: amplifier A is A1, amplifier B is A2
first-stage current into the rail side
0 V to 2 V input, referred to ground

notes: Design targets: 5 V DC supply, 0 V to 2 V DC input, 0 mA to 100 mA DC output.

circuits.title: Discrete instrumentation amplifier with attenuation for a 3.3-V ADC
circuits.description: Both halves of one OPA2188 on ±15 V form the input pair of a three-amplifier instrumentation amplifier: each buffers one side of a differential input riding on a 10 V common-mode level, and a 500 Ω RG joins their inverting inputs, each of which also takes 1 kΩ of feedback from its own output. The two outputs, VOUTP and VOUTN, feed an INA159 difference amplifier on a single 3.3 V supply, with REF1 tied to 3.3 V, REF2 to ground and SENSE to its output, giving one ground-referred output VOUT for a 3.3 V ADC.

parts.note: amplifier A and amplifier B form the input pair; the two halves carry the designators U2 and U5

notes: The input is a differential step of VDIFF split as +VDIFF/2 and -VDIFF/2 about a 10 V common-mode source referred to ground.

circuits.title: RTD amplifier with linearization
circuits.description: A Pt100 RTD to ground is excited from a 5 V REF5050 reference through 4.99 kΩ, and the RTD voltage goes to the non-inverting input of one OPA2188 amplifier. The inverting input sits on a divider of 49.1 kΩ from the reference and 1 kΩ to ground, with 60.4 kΩ of feedback from the output, so the output reads 0 V at 0°C and 5 V at 200°C. R5, 105.8 kΩ from the output back to the RTD node, adds excitation that rises with the output and straightens the RTD's curve. The REF5050 runs from +15 V, with 1 µF on its input and on its output.

parts.note: amplifier A used; amplifier B unused
linearization: positive-going excitation from the output

circuits.title: Input current protection
circuits.description: A unity-gain buffer whose input comes in through a 5 kΩ series resistor. When VIN goes past a supply rail the internal clamp diodes conduct, and the resistor holds that current to the 10 mA maximum. The resistor adds its thermal noise at the input.

parts.note: amplifier A as a voltage follower; amplifier B unused

notes: Input current through the protection diodes: 10 mA maximum.

operation.text: The OPA2188 is a dual zero-drift amplifier: it auto-zeroes (chops) its input stage to hold offset to 25 µV maximum and drift to 0.085 µV/°C maximum, with near-zero change over time. Its signal path runs through a first chopper, a transconductance stage GM1, a second chopper and a notch filter, then GM2 and the output stage GM3, with capacitors C1 and C2, and a feed-forward stage GM_FF driven from the input. The input is CMOS, with a common-mode range from V- to 1.5 V below V+, and the output swings to within 15 mV of either rail with no load.

The part works from 4 V to 36 V (±2 V to ±18 V) and has one functional mode: it is on whenever the supply is inside that range. Many parameters are specified from -40°C to +105°C. A supply above 40 V can damage it permanently.
Put 0.1 µF capacitors close to the supply pins; a noisy or high-impedance supply otherwise couples errors in. 0.1 µF is enough in most cases.
The inputs carry built-in EMI filters. EMI rejection at IN+ is measured from 10 MHz to 6 GHz. Strong RF fields can still shift the offset.

Driving an input past the linear common-mode range does not reverse the output: the output stays against the rail it was heading for. With ±18 V supplies and a 37 VPP (±18.5 V) sine at a unity-gain follower, the output clips at the rails without inverting.

Low closed-loop gain with a large capacitive load cuts phase margin and can cause peaking or oscillation. A small resistor in series with the output, 50 Ω for example, isolates a heavy capacitive load. The part drives 1 nF typical.

Every pin has internal ESD protection. The input ESD diodes also protect against input overdrive as long as the current stays at or below 10 mA; a series resistor in the driven input limits it, at the cost of its thermal noise. An ESD event becomes a short high-current pulse that the protection steers around the amplifier core and dissipates as heat. If a pin is pushed outside its operating range, some ESD cells can turn on and conduct. Where the supply may not absorb that current, zener diodes can be added on the supply pins, with a zener voltage above the normal supply so they stay off in use and below the safe supply limit so they conduct before the pin exceeds it.

Keep traces short, use a ground plane, and mount surface-mount parts right next to the pins, with 0.1 µF across the supply pins. Keep high-impedance input traces short, connect grounds to a low-impedance plane, and put the supply bypass capacitors next to the part. RFI shows up as a change in offset or DC level that follows the interfering signal; the OPA2188 has low RFI sensitivity.

In the high-side converter the input voltage and RS1 set the first-stage current, and the ratio of RS2 to RS3 fixes how many times larger the output-stage current is than the first-stage current. Low offset and low drift keep the DC error small, and the rail-to-rail output lets the amplifiers drive the MOSFET gates fully within the supply rails.
An automotive Q100-qualified version is sold as OPA2188-Q1.
